double_arithmetic_discrepancies.calcMagicSuccess_float_cast: Formulas.java:1301 explicitly casts the double result to (float) before Math.round. In IEEE 754 binary32, precision is 24 bits. The oracle models this with binary_nearest(x, 24) to guarantee exact equivalence with the Java JVM.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.calcMagicDam_sqrt: Formulas.java:845 uses Math.sqrt(mAtk). The oracle uses rational interval bounds [lo, hi] certified by integer square root (isqrt) to prove that the whole-number damage is invariant to floating-point vs exact square root.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.calcAtkBreak_sqrt: Formulas.java:1010 uses Math.sqrt(13 * dmg). The oracle similarly certifies integer interval agreement for all vectors.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.calculateKarmaLost_division: Formulas.java:1820 rounds the multiplier conversion and both divisions in binary64 before int truncation. Exact rational truncation is NOT universally equivalent: level2, XP6208133913, multiplier2.069377971 gives rational100000000 vs Java99999999. All supplied vectors model the binary64 sites with integer-only nearest/ties-even significand rounding; RateKarmaLost=1.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.resurrect_quirk_boundary: Formulas.java:1377 uses strictly greater comparison (restorePercent - baseRestorePercent > 20.0). Floating point round-off near boundary could flip this condition; rational arithmetic guarantees exactness at the 20.0 boundary.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.FuncAtkEvasion_intermediate_cast: FuncAtkEvasion.java:61 truncates intermediate evasion to (int) before modifiers. Without this intermediate truncation, rounding after modifiers produces different integer values (e.g. lvl 1 DEX 20 player yields 27 with cast vs 28 without; adding +4 modifier yields 31 vs 32; buff 1.1x yields 30 vs 31).
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.Heal_nongrade_shot_multiplier: In Phase 3 with no spiritshots, nongrade weapon or unarmed yields mAtkMul = 1 + 1 = 2 per Heal.java:89. Static healing bypasses mAtk, heal_effect and crit.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.TickHp_binary32_multiplier: AbstractEffect.java:149 converts integer ticks*666 to binary32, divides by 1000f in binary32, then widens to double. ticks5 multiplier=1745879/524288, not333/100. Integer-only binary_nearest(...,24) emulates nearest/ties-even without struct/numpy/host floats; subsequent power parsing and products use binary_nearest(...,53). HoT100 yields332 whole plus999992 Q remainder; DoT truncates before whole HP subtraction (D-R12).
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.TickHp_nonlethal_clamp: TickHp.java:75-76 caps negative DoT power at currentHp - 1, preventing death from DoT. Clamped power is non-negative and zero if currentHp <= 1.
double_arithmetic_discrepancies.getAffectLimit_unlimited_zero: Skill.java:638 returns 0 when width==0. AffectScope treats 0 as unlimited targets (affectLimit > 0 guard and .limit(affectLimit > 0 ? affectLimit : Integer.MAX_VALUE)). Fixed-limit skills require width > 0 in retail datapack.
